scope: Selected foundational sources, the main general KLS bound milestones, and the connected moment-map, slicing and thin-shell developments through July 2026; not an exhaustive bibliography or a paper-by-paper proof verification.

groups.title: Analytic foundations and selected local coverage
General KLS bounds and stochastic localization

papers.title: Convex measures on locally convex spaces
papers.result: Convex/log-concave measures, inner measure and density representation on the affine support.
papers.remaining: The locally convex-space theory and the other convexity parameters are outside our finite-dimensional log-concave scope.

papers.title: Isoperimetric problems for convex bodies and a localization lemma
papers.locator: Theorem 5.1 (Main Theorem); needle reduction of Section 2
papers.result: For every convex body K, ψ(K) ≥ ln 2 / M₁(K), with M₁ the mean distance to the centroid; for isotropic bodies this is the dimension-scale bound ψₙ = O(n^(1/2)). States the KLS conjecture. The localization lemma is quoted from Lovász–Simonovits (1993) and extended to exponential needles.
papers.remaining: No statement of the paper is formalized. The localization lemma (Lemma 2.1) is only cited, so a Lean proof needs Lovász–Simonovits (1993) or a later proof. The paper proves no Poincaré or covariance bound; with the local Cheeger inequality, Theorem 5.1 would give C_P ≤ (16 / ln² 2) E‖X − EX‖² for convex bodies, the factor 2 coming from the product denominator, once the paper's boundary measure is matched with the local outer Minkowski content.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Convex bodies in R^n with Lebesgue (uniform) measure; the isoperimetric coefficient ψ(K) uses the product denominator vol(S)·vol(K∖S)/vol(K) of (1.1), within a factor 2 of the min-denominator form (1.2).
lemma_map.omitted: Remark 2.8 is a normalization comment. The paper proves no Poincaré or trace-of-covariance bound; those appear in later literature.

items.label: Localization lemma
items.statement: For lower semicontinuous integrable g, h on R^n with positive integrals, some needle (segment with a linear weight to the power n−1) has positive g- and h-integrals.
items.note: Cited from Lovász–Simonovits (1993); its proof is not in this paper.

items.label: Four-function needle reduction
items.statement: For nonnegative continuous f1..f4 and α, β > 0, an inequality between products of integral powers holds on every convex body iff it holds on every needle.

items.label: Semicontinuous extension
items.statement: Corollary 2.2 extends to upper semicontinuous f1, f2 and lower semicontinuous f3, f4.

items.label: Needle with an equality constraint
items.statement: On a bounded open convex T, if ∫g > 0 and ∫h = 0 for bounded lower semicontinuous g and continuous h, some needle in T has positive g-integral and zero h-integral.

items.label: Non-strict version
items.statement: Strict inequalities in Corollary 2.4 may be replaced by non-strict ones.

items.label: One-dimensional log-concave reduction
items.statement: On an interval, a four-function inequality holds for every log-concave weight iff it holds for every exponential weight on every subinterval.

items.label: Exponential needles
items.statement: For nonnegative continuous f1..f4 on R^n, the four-function inequality holds for every compactly supported log-concave F iff it holds on every exponential needle.

items.label: Reverse Hölder for linear functions
items.statement: For 0 < p < q there is C(p, q), independent of n and K, with ‖f‖_q ≤ C(p, q)‖f‖_p for every linear f on a convex body K.

items.label: Isotropic body contains and is contained in balls
items.statement: An isotropic convex body satisfies √((n+2)/n) B ⊆ K ⊆ √(n(n+2)) B.

items.label: Isoperimetric coefficient bound
items.statement: For every convex body K, ψ(K) ≥ ln 2 / M₁(K), where M₁ is the mean distance to the centroid.
items.note: Convex bodies only; the later log-concave version is quoted as Theorem 5.11 of Milman (2009).

items.label: Three-set partition form
items.statement: If K = K1 ∪ K2 ∪ K3 with dist(K1, K2) ≥ ε > 0, then ε·vol(K1)·vol(K2) ≤ vol(K)·vol(K3)·M₁(K)/ln 2.

items.label: Bound by the mean chord length
items.statement: ψ(K) ≥ 1/χ(K), where χ(K) averages the longest chord of K centred at each point.

items.label: KLS conjecture
items.statement: ψ(K) is of order 1/√a(K), where a(K) is the largest eigenvalue of the inertia matrix.
items.note: The repository states a covariance-normalized Poincaré version for log-concave laws (KLS.Conjecture); it is not a literal form of this convex-body conjecture.

items.label: Upper bound by hyperplane cuts
items.statement: ψ(K) ≤ 10/√a(K) for every convex body K.

items.label: Hyperplane cut through the centroid
items.statement: For b(K) = 0 and a unit vector u, the two halves of K cut by u^⊥ satisfy a product-volume bound against the section area and β = E(u·x)².

papers.title: Isoperimetric and analytic inequalities for log-concave probability measures
papers.result: Cheeger/Poincaré inequalities for log-concave laws; the one-dimensional comparison yields C_P ≤ 12 Var.
papers.remaining: Our one-dimensional proof uses a different analytic argument. The paper’s general isoperimetric theory is not fully formalized.

local_results.scope: One-dimensional upper bound, now strengthened locally to 4 Var; the independent 12 Var proof is retained

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Absolutely continuous log-concave probability measures on R^n; μ⁺ is the Minkowski boundary measure; Is(μ) is the min-denominator Cheeger constant h, λ₁ = 1/C_P is the spectral gap and ρ the log-Sobolev constant.
lemma_map.omitted: The displayed consequences (1.8), (2.7), (2.8) and (2.10) are recorded with the statements they follow from.

items.label: Perimeter, entropy and ball mass
items.statement: For log-concave μ on R^n, every measurable A, x₀ and r > 0: 2rμ⁺(A) ≥ μ(A)log(1/μ(A)) + (1 − μ(A))log(1/(1 − μ(A))) + log μ{|x − x₀| ≤ r}.

items.label: Cheeger bound by the L² radius
items.statement: Is(μ) ≥ 1/(K‖|x − x₀|‖_{L²(μ)}) with x₀ the barycenter and K universal; hence λ₁ ≥ 1/(4K²‖|x − x₀|‖²_{L²}) by Cheeger.
items.note: The proof gives Is(μ) ≥ 1/(6r) with r the 2/3-quantile of |x − x₀| (3.3).

items.label: Gaussian isoperimetry, log-Sobolev and Gaussian moments
items.statement: For log-concave μ, Gaussian-type isoperimetry, a log-Sobolev inequality and ∫exp(ε|x|²)dμ < ∞ are equivalent, with ρ ≥ 1/(K‖|x − x₀|‖²_ψ) for ψ(u) = exp(u²) − 1.

items.label: Functional form of Theorem 1.1
items.statement: For locally Lipschitz f with values in [0, 1] and a symmetric convex body B: 2∫‖∇f‖_{B°}dμ ≥ Ent(f) + Ent(1 − f) + log μ(B(x₀)).
items.note: Proved by the Prékopa–Leindler inequality.

items.label: Measures supported in a ball
items.statement: If μ is concentrated in a ball of radius r, then 2r∫|∇f|dμ ≥ Ent(f) + Ent(1 − f) and 2rμ⁺(A) ≥ μ(A)log(1/μ(A)) + (1 − μ(A))log(1/(1 − μ(A))); hence Is(μ) ≥ log 2/r and λ₁ ≥ log²2/(4r²).

items.label: Log-Sobolev versus spectral gap in a ball
items.statement: If μ is concentrated in a ball of radius r, then λ₁/(1 + 2r√λ₁) ≤ ρ ≤ λ₁, so ρ ≥ 1/(10r²).

items.label: Borell's lemma
items.statement: For symmetric convex B with θ = μ(B) > 1/2 and t ≥ 1: 1 − μ(tB) ≤ (1 − θ)((1 − θ)/θ)^((t−1)/2).

items.label: Functional Gaussian isoperimetry
items.statement: If μ⁺(A) ≥ cI(μ(A)) for the Gaussian isoperimetric function I, then c[I(∫f) − ∫I(f)] ≤ ∫|∇f| for locally Lipschitz f with values in [0, 1].

items.label: Gaussian isoperimetry gives log-Sobolev
items.statement: Inequality (3.10) implies (c²/2)Ent(f²) ≤ ∫|∇f|² dμ.

items.label: Cheeger constant on the line
items.statement: For log-concave μ on R: 1/(3Var) ≤ Is²(μ) ≤ 2/Var, with equality cases the uniform and two-sided exponential laws; Is(μ) = 2f(m) at the median.
items.note: Locally only weaker bounds are proved: Ψ² ≤ 12 C_P on the line and Ψ² ≤ π C_P in general, which with C_P ≤ 4 Var do not give the constant 3.

items.label: Hensley-type section ratio
items.statement: For a convex body satisfying the isotropy condition, central sections by hyperplanes cutting B into equal volumes have ratio at most √6.

items.label: Spectral gap on the line
items.statement: For log-concave μ on R: 1/(12 Var) ≤ λ₁ ≤ 1/Var, i.e. Var ≤ C_P ≤ 12 Var.
items.note: Sharper upper constant C_P ≤ 4 Var, proved by a different argument that does not use Proposition 4.1; the paper's 12 Var follows as a corollary, and Var ≤ C_P is the linear test.

items.label: Log-Sobolev constant on the line
items.statement: For log-concave μ on R: 1/(24‖ξ − Eξ‖²_ψ) ≤ ρ ≤ 8/(3‖ξ − Eξ‖²_ψ) with ψ(x) = exp(x²) − 1.

items.label: Cheeger bound for norms
items.statement: For a random vector X with log-concave law in a normed space, Is(μ_X) ≥ 1/(6r) with r the 2/3-quantile of ‖X‖, where μ_X is the law of ‖X‖.

items.label: Small-ball monotonicity
items.statement: With F(t) = P(‖X‖ ≤ t), the function F(t)/t^(1/(2e)) is nondecreasing where 0 < F(t) ≤ e/(e + 1).

papers.title: On the role of convexity in isoperimetry, spectral gap and concentration
papers.result: Under convexity, isoperimetry, spectral gap and concentration control one another up to universal constants.
papers.remaining: The full equivalence remains open locally; our forward infimum comparison is supporting infrastructure, not this theorem.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Metric probability spaces; "convexity assumptions" mean total-variation limits of weighted Riemannian manifolds with Ric + Hess ψ ≥ 0. D_Che is the min-denominator Cheeger constant h and D_Poin = 1/√C_P, so D_Poin ≥ D_Che/2 is C_P ≤ 4Ψ². Attributed statements are quoted from the cited authors.
lemma_map.omitted: Remarks 3.3, 4.4, 5.13, 6.3 and 6.7 are expository; the unnumbered regularity theorems for isoperimetric minimizers in the appendix are quoted background.

items.label: Cheeger constant D_Che
items.statement: Best D with Ĩ(t) ≥ D t on [0, 1/2], where Ĩ is the isoperimetric profile.
items.note: Finite-dimensional laws on their affine support, with outer Minkowski content.

items.label: Poincaré constant D_Poin
items.statement: Best D with D‖f − Ef‖₂ ≤ ‖|∇f|‖₂ for Lipschitz-on-balls f.
items.note: Stored as C_P = D_Poin^(−2) for finite-dimensional laws.

items.label: Exponential concentration D_Exp
items.statement: Best D with μ(|f − Ef| ≥ t) ≤ e·exp(−Dt) for 1-Lipschitz f.

items.label: First-moment concentration D_FM
items.statement: Best D with ‖f − Ef‖₁ ≤ 1/D for 1-Lipschitz f.

items.label: Cheeger inequality
items.statement: D_Poin ≥ D_Che/2.
items.note: Proved as C_P ≤ 4Ψ² for finite-dimensional log-concave laws; the paper states it on general metric probability spaces.

items.label: Poincaré implies exponential concentration
items.statement: D_Exp ≥ c·D_Poin for a universal c.

items.label: Buser inequality on closed manifolds
items.statement: For uniform measure on a closed manifold with Ric ≥ 0, D_Che ≥ c·D_Poin.

items.label: Buser–Ledoux inequality
items.statement: Under smooth convexity assumptions, D_Che ≥ c·D_Poin.
items.note: Euclidean case only, as Ψ² ≤ π C_P, i.e. c = 1/√π, for every finite-dimensional log-concave law including nonsmooth ones; weighted manifolds are not covered.

items.label: Cheeger, Poincaré and concentration are equivalent
items.statement: Under convexity assumptions, D_Che ≃ D_Poin ≃ D_Exp ≃ D_FM up to universal constants.

items.label: Lipschitz-distance form of D_Che
items.statement: D_Che ≃ inf over A with μ(A) ≥ 1/2 of 1/∫d(x, A)dμ.

items.label: Stability of D_Che for convex domains
items.statement: If vol(K ∩ L) ≥ v_K vol(K) and ≥ v_L vol(L), then D_Che(K) ≥ c·v_K²/log(1 + 1/v_L)·D_Che(L).

items.label: Concavity of the isoperimetric profile
items.statement: Under generalized smooth convexity the isoperimetric profile is concave on (0, 1); I^(n/(n−1)) is concave for uniform measures.

items.label: Mean versus median in Orlicz norms
items.statement: ½‖f − Ef‖_N ≤ ‖f − Mf‖_N ≤ 3‖f − Ef‖_N for every Orlicz norm.

items.label: Cheeger as an L¹ Poincaré inequality
items.statement: Cheeger's inequality with D_Che holds iff D_Che‖f − Mf‖₁ ≤ ‖|∇f|‖₁ for all f.

items.label: Metric gradient
items.statement: On metric probability spaces |∇f|(x) is the limsup of |f(y) − f(x)|/d(x, y) as y → x, and 0 at isolated points.
items.note: Same convention, including isolated points.

items.label: All (p, q) Poincaré inequalities are equivalent
items.statement: Under convexity assumptions, D_{p,q} ≤ C p′ D_{p′,q′} for 1 ≤ p ≤ q ≤ ∞ and 1 ≤ p′ ≤ q′ ≤ ∞.

items.label: Monotonicity of (p, q) constants
items.statement: If 1/p − 1/q = 1/p′ − 1/q′ with p ≤ p′, q ≤ q′, then D_{p′,q′} ≥ (p/p′) D_{p,q}, without convexity.

items.label: Maz'ya–Cheeger inequality, new proof
items.statement: D_Poin ≥ D_Che/2.
items.note: Same Lean result as Theorem 1.1, by a different proof; finite-dimensional log-concave laws only.

items.label: Gromov–Milman inequality, new proof
items.statement: D_Exp ≥ c·D_Poin.

items.label: Concentration from (r, r) Poincaré
items.statement: D_Exp ≥ c_r D_{r,r} for every r ≥ 1.

items.label: Poincaré versus profile decay
items.statement: Under smooth convexity, a (p, q) Poincaré inequality is equivalent to Ĩ(t) ≥ D′ t^r with r = 1 + 1/p − 1/q in [1/2, 2], with comparable constants.

items.label: L¹-type Poincaré versus isoperimetry
items.statement: For 0 < r ≤ 1, the (1/r, 1) Poincaré inequality is equivalent to Ĩ(t) ≥ D t^r, without convexity.

items.label: Uniform measures strengthen the results
items.statement: For uniform measures, concavity of I^(n/(n−1)) upgrades the main theorem to an (n/(n−1), 1) Poincaré inequality.

items.label: Reverse local Poincaré inequality
items.statement: Under Ric + Hess ψ ≥ −K, c(t)|∇P_t f|² ≤ P_t(f²) − (P_t f)² pointwise, with c(t) = 2t when K = 0.
items.note: K = 0 for smooth convex potentials on Euclidean spaces, integrated against nonnegative C_c^∞ tests (a.e. form for bounded data).

items.label: L¹ heat displacement
items.note: Indicator data of smooth domains with relative perimeter, smooth convex potential; a sharper coefficient 2√(t/π) is also proved.

items.label: Paley–Zygmund-type quantile bound
items.statement: If ‖f‖₂ ≤ D‖f‖₁ then the (1 − ε) quantile of |f| is at least θ‖f‖₁ with ε = (1 − θ)²/D².

items.label: Optimal 1-Lipschitz functions behave like linear ones
items.statement: An essentially optimal 1-Lipschitz f₀ for first-moment concentration has ‖f₀‖_Ψ₁ ≤ C₀‖f₀‖₁ and a quantile lower bound.

items.label: Slow tail decay suffices
items.statement: An arbitrarily slow uniform tail decay of 1-Lipschitz functions implies the main theorem's statements with constants depending only on the decay.

items.label: Going down to a large convex subset
items.statement: If L ⊆ K is convex with vol(L) ≥ v vol(K), then D_FM(L) ≥ c/log(1 + 1/v)·D_Exp(K).

items.label: Going up to a convex superset
items.statement: If L ⊆ K are convex with vol(L) ≥ v vol(K), then D_Che(K) ≥ v² D_Che(L).

items.label: Stability under Banach–Mazur-close bodies
items.statement: If d_G(K, L) ≤ 1 + s/n for 1 ≤ s ≤ C₁n, then D_Che(K) and D_Che(L) agree up to a factor C₂ s.

items.label: Log-concave version of Lemmas 5.1–5.2
items.statement: Lemmas 5.1 and 5.2 hold for absolutely continuous log-concave measures with density domination dμ_K/dx ≥ v dμ_L/dx.

items.label: Total-variation stability of D_Che
items.statement: If d_TV(μ₁, μ₂) ≤ 1 − ε for log-concave μ₁, μ₂, their Cheeger constants agree up to c(ε) = c′ε²/log(1 + 1/ε).

items.label: Optimality of the stability exponent
items.statement: Products of cubes and ℓ₁-balls show the quadratic dependence in Theorem 1.7 is necessary.

items.label: Optimality of Corollary 5.3
items.statement: Truncated ℓ₁-balls show the linear dependence on s in Corollary 5.3 is necessary.

items.label: Sharper stability near the Euclidean ball
items.statement: Near B₂ⁿ the bound in Corollary 5.3 improves to 1/(C₂√s).

items.label: Lipschitz-on-average transport
items.statement: If T pushes μ to ν and ν satisfies convexity assumptions, then D_Che(ν) ≥ c/∫‖DT‖_op dμ·D_Che(μ).

items.label: Diameter bound for convex domains
items.statement: For locally convex smooth K with Ric ≥ 0, D_Poin ≥ π/(2 diam K), and π/diam K in Euclidean space.

items.label: KLS first-moment bound
items.statement: For log-concave μ on R^n, D_Che(μ) ≥ c/∫|x − x₀|dμ for every x₀.

items.label: First-moment bound under convexity assumptions
items.statement: Under convexity assumptions, D_Che ≥ c/∫d(x, x₀)dμ for every x₀.

items.label: Mean chord bound
items.statement: For log-concave μ with bounded support B, D_Che(μ) ≥ c/∫θ_B dμ, θ_B the longest symmetric chord.

items.label: Variance-of-norm bound
items.statement: For log-concave μ, D_Che(μ) ≥ c/Var_μ(|x − x₀|²)^(1/4).

items.label: Uniform bound for ℓ_p balls
items.statement: Normalized ℓ_pⁿ balls with p ∈ [1, 2] have D_Che bounded below uniformly in n.

items.label: Profile lower semicontinuity from above
items.statement: If μ_m tends to μ from above, liminf of I_{μ_m}(t) is at least the lower limit of I_μ near t.

items.label: Profile lower semicontinuity from within
items.statement: The same conclusion when μ_m tends to μ from within.

items.label: Profile versus capacity
items.statement: inf over [a, b] of I ≤ Cap₁(a, b) ≤ inf over [a, b) of I.

items.label: Profile symmetry
items.statement: If I is lower semicontinuous at t and 1 − t, then I(t) = I(1 − t).

items.label: Upper semicontinuity under concavity
items.statement: If μ_m → μ in total variation with concave profiles, the lower limit of I_μ near t dominates limsup I_{μ_m}(t).

items.label: Convergence of profiles
items.statement: Under total-variation convergence from above or within, with concave profiles, I_{μ_m}(t) converges to the lower limit of I_μ near t.

items.label: Hölder continuity of the profile
items.statement: For densities bounded above on balls, the profile is absolutely continuous and locally (n−1)/n-Hölder.

items.label: Approximation preserves concavity
items.statement: Smooth convex approximations from above or within give pointwise profile convergence, so the limit profile is concave.

items.label: Convex bodies satisfy the assumptions
items.statement: Uniform measures on convex domains satisfy the convexity assumptions, with I and I^(n/(n−1)) concave.

items.label: Log-concave measures satisfy the assumptions
items.statement: Absolutely continuous log-concave measures on R^n satisfy the convexity assumptions, with concave profile.

items.label: Borell-type tail bound
items.statement: If μ_m(B(x₀, R)) = θ > 1/2, then μ_m(M ∖ B(x₀, tR)) ≤ θ((1 − θ)/θ)^((t+1)/2) for t ≥ 1.

items.label: Riemannian Prékopa–Leindler
items.statement: Under Ric + Hess ψ ≥ 0, the weighted Prékopa–Leindler inequality holds along geodesic interpolation.

items.label: Concavity for uniform measures
items.statement: For locally convex smooth domains in manifolds with Ric ≥ 0, I and I^(n/(n−1)) are concave.

items.label: Concavity for weighted manifolds
items.statement: Under Ric + Hess ψ ≥ 0 the profile is concave.

items.label: Concavity on locally convex domains
items.statement: On locally convex C² domains with Ric + Hess ψ ≥ 0 the profile is concave.

items.label: One-dimensional log-concave profile
items.statement: For absolutely continuous log-concave μ on R, the isoperimetric profile is concave on (0, 1).

items.label: Half-lines are minimizers
items.statement: In dimension one the minimizers are half-lines, so I(t) = min(F′∘F⁻¹(t), F′∘F⁻¹(1 − t)).

papers.title: Interpolating thin-shell and sharp large-deviation estimates for isotropic log-concave measures
papers.result: Quantitative radial concentration across thin-shell and large-deviation scales for isotropic log-concave laws.
papers.remaining: Radial deviation estimates and their thin-shell/isoperimetric consequences are not locally formalized.

papers.title: Thin shell implies spectral gap up to polylog via a stochastic localization scheme
papers.result: Introduces stochastic localization and transfers thin-shell control to KLS with logarithmic losses.
papers.remaining: The stochastic process, its covariance estimates and the transfer theorem are not locally formalized.

papers.title: Density of Lipschitz functions and equivalence of weak gradients in metric measure spaces
papers.result: Identifies weak-gradient notions and relaxed energies in metric measure spaces.
papers.remaining: The general metric-space theorem and unrestricted singular-law comparison are not formalized here. Our absolutely-continuous Euclidean identity is an independent restricted counterpart.

local_results.scope: Intrinsic absolutely-continuous E^can = 2 Ch in the local-slope convention

papers.title: Analysis and Geometry of Markov Diffusion Operators
papers.locator: Proposition 4.3.1; Gaussian Poincaré and Dirichlet-form background
papers.result: Tensorization and Gaussian functional inequalities within the diffusion/Dirichlet-form framework.
papers.remaining: The full diffusion, semigroup and Γ-calculus theory is not covered by our selected results.

local_results.scope: Finite Hilbert-product constants, including empty products

papers.title: Logarithmically-concave moment measures I
papers.result: Develops the Hessian metric and weighted Poincaré structure associated with log-concave moment measures.
papers.remaining: Moment-map existence/regularity, the Hessian metric and weighted geometric identities are not locally formalized.

papers.title: Moment measures
papers.result: A nonzero finite centered measure whose support spans the space is the moment measure of an essentially continuous convex potential, unique up to translation.
papers.remaining: The existence/uniqueness theorem is not locally formalized; generic closed forms do not supply its convex potential.

papers.title: Approaching the Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits and variance conjectures
papers.locator: Page 11; local source audit linked below
papers.result: Records C_P ≤ 4 tr(Cov), whose one-dimensional specialization is 4 Var, in a broader account of KLS and the variance conjecture.
papers.remaining: Only the one-dimensional bound is formalized here, by an independent proof. The high-dimensional trace bound, its original exact-constant attribution and optimality over all laws are not certified.

local_results.scope: One-dimensional 4 Var upper bound, including zero variance

papers.title: Perimeter as relaxed Minkowski content in metric measure spaces
papers.result: A Minkowski coarea inequality and identification of relaxed Minkowski content with BV perimeter.
papers.remaining: The complete lower/upper content, recovery and relaxation chain is formalized for finite Borel measures on arbitrary metric spaces. The new continuation proves the globally Lipschitz/global L1 bounded-support reduction of Remark 3.4 for every measurable finite-mass target under any Borel measure, the direct positive-level local-slope coarea upper bound under finite mass of a positive-support neighborhood (all levels for nonnegative functions), and perimeter at most lower content at measurable finite-mass targets. Under finiteness on bounded Borel sets, actual bounded measurable lower-recovery sets have finite mass and finite lower content term by term; indicators converge globally in L1 and lower contents converge to perimeter. The existing relaxed lower-content set infimum equals the perimeter at Theorem 3.6's measurable finite-mass target scope, including infinite perimeter and infinite total mass; convergence ensures eventual finite approximating-set masses without changing the class or excluding infinite-mass finite prefixes. Finite target mass and finite lower content imply a finite-mass positive neighborhood. Actual lower-to-upper radius recovery holds there, and a diagonal sequence gives bounded open upper-recovery sets with finite masses/contents and original global indicator L1 convergence. The existing relaxed upper infimum equals perimeter, hence the lower relaxation, at the published finite-mass target scope, including infinite perimeter by order. The full Lemma 3.2 chain is formalized with the actual right-radius liminf of integrated open-ball growth under nonnegativity and finite positive-support-neighborhood mass. Lemma 2.1 exposes the actual relaxed-upper <= lower-content bound at finite-mass Borel targets under any measure. Lemma 2.1's relaxed lower/upper-content equality is also formalized for every Borel measure at measurable finite-mass targets, and on proper metric spaces Remark 3.5's locally Lipschitz classes with global or compact-set L1 convergence have relaxation infima equal to the bounded-support perimeter at measurable finite-mass targets for every Borel measure (2026-10-01). The locally Lipschitz classes on nonproper spaces, nonconvex ambient/support transfer and general RCD comparisons remain pending. These local Lean results do not add ledger certificates; remote Lean verification is a separate check.

local_results.scope: Minkowski coarea inequality in the local Euclidean scope

Published finite-mass target / finite-on-bounded measure scope: bounded-support reduction, full coarea radius chain, lower-to-upper recovery, both actual recoveries and both relaxed identities; convex closed-support Cheeger identification

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Metric space with a Borel measure finite on bounded Borel sets; contents are defined for Borel sets of finite measure.
lemma_map.omitted: Remarks 3.1, 4.1 and 4.4 are expository (literature context, Euclidean background and a cited counterexample) and are not separate formalization targets.

items.label: Lower content bounds relaxed upper content
items.statement: For a Borel set A of finite measure, the relaxed upper Minkowski content is at most the lower Minkowski content.
items.note: Holds for every Borel measure; the standing finiteness on bounded sets is not needed.

items.label: Relaxed lower and upper contents agree
items.statement: The relaxed lower and upper Minkowski contents coincide.
items.note: Measurable finite-mass targets under every Borel measure.

items.label: Minkowski coarea inequality
items.statement: For a nonnegative Lipschitz f with a finite-mass neighbourhood of {f > 0}, the integrated lower content of superlevel sets is at most the liminf of the integrated open-ball growth, which is at most the slope integral.
items.note: Both inequalities of the chain, with the actual open-ball supremum semigroup.

items.label: Perimeter by Lipschitz relaxation
items.statement: Per(A) is the infimum of liminf of slope integrals over Lipschitz approximants converging to the indicator of A in L¹.
items.note: The library perimeter uses bounded-support tests; lipschitzRelaxation_eq_perimeter_of_measure_lt_top identifies the two at finite-mass targets.

items.label: Truncation and bounded-support reduction
items.statement: Only approximants with values in [0, 1] and bounded positivity set need to be considered in Definition 3.3.
items.note: Measurable finite-mass targets under every Borel measure.

items.label: Locally Lipschitz variants agree
items.statement: The locally Lipschitz variants of the perimeter (L¹ or L¹_loc convergence) agree with Definition 3.3 on proper spaces, and on complete separable spaces by a non-elementary argument.
items.note: Proper spaces only. The complete separable case, cited from Di Marino's thesis, is not formalized.

items.label: Relaxed Minkowski content equals perimeter
items.statement: For every Borel set A with finite measure, the relaxed lower Minkowski content equals Per(A) of Definition 3.3.
items.note: The exact statement is the composition of these two declarations under the standing assumption. No single declaration states it yet and no certificate is registered, so the paper is not covered.

items.label: Coarea with lower content
items.statement: Under the regularity assumption (4.2), the total variation of a nonnegative Lipschitz f equals the integrated lower content of its superlevel sets; lower content equals perimeter for almost every level, and lower and upper contents agree for unit-slope functions.
items.note: Needs the BV total variation of functions and the Fleming–Rishel coarea formula (4.1), which the paper cites.

items.label: Distance-function level sets
items.statement: Under a length assumption and (4.2), almost every level set of a distance function has equal lower content, upper content and perimeter, and has a Minkowski content.

items.label: Doubling coarea with Hausdorff gauge
items.statement: For a doubling measure and nonnegative Lipschitz f with finite-mass positivity set, the integrated gauge-Hausdorff measure of B ∩ {f = t} is bounded by the asymptotic Lipschitz integral and by twice the slope integral over B.
items.note: Needs the Carathéodory gauge measure and Vitali covering for doubling measures.

items.label: Perimeter lower bound on level sets
items.statement: On complete doubling spaces satisfying (4.2), almost every superlevel set has finite perimeter with perimeter measure at least half the gauge-Hausdorff measure on its essential boundary.

papers.title: Eldan’s stochastic localization and the KLS conjecture: Isoperimetry, concentration and mixing
papers.result: For isotropic log-concave laws, C_P = O(n^(1/2)), equivalently ψₙ = O(n^(1/4)); the paper also studies mixing and concentration.
papers.remaining: The quantitative localization theorem, covariance bounds and mixing results are not locally formalized.

papers.title: The Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture
papers.result: A guide to KLS formulations, geometric consequences and algorithmic motivation at the 2018 frontier.
papers.remaining: Use for orientation; its historical frontier is superseded by the later papers in the frontier table.

papers.title: Stein kernels and moment maps
papers.result: Constructs Stein kernels using moment maps, connecting Hessian geometry to probabilistic identities.
papers.remaining: The canonical moment-map Stein kernel is not locally formalized.

papers.title: An almost constant lower bound of the isoperimetric coefficient in the KLS conjecture
papers.locator: Main bound, translated from the lower-bound convention for h
papers.result: ψₙ ≤ exp(C√(log n · log log n)) = n^o(1); hence C_P = n^o(1), breaking the polynomial barrier.
papers.remaining: The stochastic-localization bootstrap and the subpolynomial bound are not locally formalized.

papers.title: Sharp Cheeger–Buser type inequalities in RCD(K,∞) spaces
papers.locator: Cheeger–Buser comparison; log-concave specialization in Letwin, introduction
papers.result: Provides the sharp reverse-comparison input used to normalize ψ² and C_P; in the log-concave convention, 1/4 ≤ ψ²/C_P ≤ π.
papers.remaining: The numerical comparison is formalized for finite-dimensional log-concave laws. For the bounded-support metric BV test class, complement symmetry for finite measures, the half-mass/symmetric equality, the BV–Minkowski Cheeger identification for probability laws on normed spaces, and, for finite-dimensional log-concave laws, the identification of the BV Cheeger constant on the closed intrinsic support with the isoperimetric constant are formalized. Test-class equivalence is formalized for finite Borel measures (global Lipschitz/global L¹), and on proper spaces also for locally Lipschitz/global or compact-local L¹ approximants. The test-class comparison beyond this scope, constant identification on nonconvex supports, and the paper's RCD(K,∞) theorem remain unformalized.

local_results.scope: Both numerical inequalities for every finite-dimensional log-concave probability law, including zero-dimensional affine support and extended optima
Closed-support BV Cheeger constant equals the isoperimetric constant for finite-dimensional log-concave laws

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: RCD(K, ∞) metric measure spaces; h(X) is the min-denominator Cheeger constant and λ₁ = 1/C_P the spectral gap (λ₀ the bottom of the spectrum when m(X) = ∞). Finite-dimensional log-concave laws on Euclidean spaces are RCD(0, ∞) with m(X) = 1. Unnumbered proof steps (46) and (48) are listed because local Lean results state them.
lemma_map.omitted: Remark 1.3 (discreteness of the spectrum) is expository.

items.label: Sharp implicit Buser inequality
items.statement: On RCD(K, ∞) spaces with m(X) = 1, h(X) ≥ sup over t > 0 of (1 − e^(−λ₁t))/J_K(t), sharp for the Gaussian when K > 0; with m(X) = ∞, h(X) ≥ 2 sup (1 − e^(−λ₀t))/J_K(t). Here J₀(t) = 2√t/√π.
items.note: No implicit (supremum over t) form is stated locally; only the explicit π bound of Corollary 1.2 is proved, in the Euclidean log-concave case.

items.label: Explicit Buser inequalities
items.statement: For K > 0 and K/λ₁ ≥ c: λ₁ ≤ (π/2c)h²; for K = 0 and m(X) = 1: λ₁ ≤ (4/π)h² inf_T T/(1 − e^(−T))² < πh²; explicit bounds for K < 0 and for infinite measure.
items.note: The K = 0, m(X) = 1 case in its weaker displayed form λ₁ ≤ πh², i.e. Ψ² ≤ π C_P, for every finite-dimensional log-concave law; the sharper constant (4/π) inf_T T/(1 − e^(−T))², the K ≠ 0 cases and infinite measure are not formalized.

items.label: CD(K, ∞) condition
items.statement: Entropy is K-convex along some W₂-geodesic between any two measures of finite entropy.

items.label: RCD(K, ∞) condition
items.statement: CD(K, ∞) together with a quadratic Cheeger energy.

items.label: Isoperimetric gradient bound for the heat flow
items.statement: For f with values in [0, 1]: |D(H_t f)|² ≤ j_K(t)([I(H_t f)]² − [H_t(I(f))]²) with I the Gaussian isoperimetric profile; hence ‖|D H_t f|‖_∞ ≤ √(2/π)√(j_K(t))‖f‖_∞, with j₀(t) = 1/(2t).
items.note: Not stated locally. The local reverse Poincaré inequality gives |∇P_t f| ≤ ‖f‖_∞/√(2t), a weaker constant for the L^∞ gradient bound.

items.label: Spectral heat decay
items.statement: For mean-zero f ∈ L²: ‖H_t f‖₂ ≤ e^(−λ₁t)‖f‖₂.
items.note: Squared form with C = 1/λ₁ for the weighted-gradient heat semigroup of a smooth convex tilted law.

items.label: L¹ heat displacement with J_K
items.statement: ‖f − H_t f‖₁ ≤ J_K(t)‖|Df|‖₁ for bounded Lipschitz f.
items.note: K = 0 coefficient J₀(t) = 2√(t/π), for indicator data of smooth domains with relative perimeter under a smooth convex potential.

items.label: Monotone auxiliary function (K > 0)
items.statement: f₁(x) = √x / arctan(√(e^(Tx) − 1)) is increasing on (0, ∞) with f₁ ≥ 1/√T.

items.label: Monotone auxiliary function (K < 0)
items.statement: f₂(x) = √x / log(e^(Tx) + √(e^(2Tx) − 1)) is decreasing on (0, ∞).

items.label: Bound under a lower bound on K/λ₁
items.statement: If K/λ₁ ≥ −c, an explicit lower bound for h(X) in terms of √λ₁ and c follows from Theorem 1.1 and Lemma 3.3.

items.label: Coarea inequality
items.statement: On a complete metric space with a measure finite on bounded sets, for bounded Lipschitz u ≥ 0 with M = sup u: ∫₀^M Per({u > t})dt ≤ ∫|∇u|dm, and almost every {u > t} has finite perimeter.
items.note: Finite measures and closed superlevel sets {u ≥ t}, for every globally Lipschitz u; the local-finiteness case is not stated in this form.

items.label: Cheeger inequality on metric measure spaces
items.statement: On a complete metric space with a measure finite on bounded sets: λ₁ ≥ h²/4 if m(X) < ∞, and λ₀ ≥ h²/4 if m(X) = ∞.
items.note: Finite-dimensional log-concave probability laws only, as C_P ≤ 4Ψ².

papers.title: Bourgain’s slicing problem and KLS isoperimetry up to polylog
papers.result: First polylogarithmic KLS bound: ψₙ = O((log n)^5), hence C_P = O((log n)^10).
papers.remaining: The localization covariance window and spectral argument are not locally formalized.

papers.title: A slightly improved bound for the KLS constant
papers.result: Improves the logarithmic exponent: ψₙ = O((log n)^3.2226), hence C_P = O((log n)^6.4452).
papers.remaining: The refined localization growth estimate and resulting bound are not locally formalized.

papers.title: Logarithmic bounds for isoperimetry and slices of convex sets
papers.result: ψₙ = O(√log n), hence C_P = O(log n), using an improved log-concave Lichnerowicz inequality.
papers.remaining: The improved Lichnerowicz estimate and stochastic localization remain unformalized locally.

papers.title: A note on Bourgain’s slicing problem
papers.result: Obtains an iterated-logarithmic slicing bound and localization estimates used in the later slicing and thin-shell work.
papers.remaining: The covariance process and Guan’s estimates are not locally formalized.

papers.title: Affirmative resolution of Bourgain’s slicing problem using Guan’s bound
papers.result: Every volume-one convex body has a hyperplane section of volume at least a universal positive constant. This resolves slicing, not KLS.
papers.remaining: The slicing theorem, M-ellipsoids and entropy-stability inputs are not locally formalized.

papers.title: The slicing conjecture via small ball estimates
papers.result: An alternative proof of slicing via small-ball estimates and Guan’s localization bound.
papers.remaining: The small-ball argument and slicing conclusion are not locally formalized.

papers.title: Isoperimetric inequalities in high-dimensional convex sets
papers.result: A detailed entry point to stochastic localization, KLS and slicing up to the period covered by the notes.
papers.remaining: Reading guide; the July 2026 frontier requires the newer sources in the frontier table.

papers.title: Thin-shell bounds via parallel coupling
papers.result: For isotropic log-concave X, E(‖X‖ − √n)² ≤ C with a universal constant, via parallel coupling.
papers.remaining: The coupling construction and dimension-free thin-shell theorem are not locally formalized; thin shell alone does not remove the KLS logarithms.

papers.title: Digesting the proof of the sharp thin-shell inequality
papers.result: For isotropic log-concave X: Var(‖X‖²) ≤ 8n and ‖T₃(X)‖²_HS ≤ 4n. The constants are sharp.
papers.remaining: The moment-Hessian estimate, third-order tensor identities and sharp conclusions are not locally formalized. A trace bound is not a universal matrix bound.

papers.title: The KLS constant is O(log^(1/4) n)
papers.result: For isotropic log-concave X and symmetric M, Var(XᵀMX) ≤ 8‖M‖²_HS = 2 E‖∇(XᵀMX)‖². For n ≥ 2, ψₙ = O((log n)^(1/4)), hence C_P = O(√log n).
papers.remaining: The quadratic inequality, its moment-map/Stein proof and the κₙ-to-KLS conversion are not locally formalized. Quadratic tests do not suffice for full KLS.
